title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 6-8): Grothendieck is developing an axiomatics of 'ateliers'. These are sets A carrying combinatorial structure: a relation ◁, a relation ≪, a 'support' map |·|, and closure operations such as '∘c'. The model examples are 'Figurations(E)' of a set E and 'maquettes'. Morphisms are partial maps, encoded as pointed maps f̂: A ⊔ {φ} → A' ⊔ {φ} with φ ↦ φ, where φ is a null element. The previous page defines Ker f = {x ∈ A | f(x) = φ}. It notes that one axiom (b) forces Ker f to be closed under ∘c, and it asks the converse question. Given a part N ⊂ A closed under ∘c, is N the kernel of a morphism, and can that morphism be chosen canonically?

This page formulates the canonical version as a universal property. We want a quotient atelier A/N with p: A → A/N annihilating N. Grothendieck hesitates whether p should annihilate exactly N or something ⊃N. The requirement is that every morphism f: A → A' annihilating N factors uniquely through p. That is, p should be the cokernel of the inclusion of N in the pointed category of ateliers with partial morphisms.

The NB makes the notion of morphism precise. A morphism is a pointed map f̂: A ⊔ {φ} → A' ⊔ {φ} sending φ to φ. The axioms imposed in the construction of Â = A ⊔ {φ} amount to saying that f̂ is compatible with ◁, ≪ and |·| on Â. This is the standard identification of partial maps with pointed maps, i.e. the Kleisli category of the Maybe monad.

The 'exemple type' takes A = Figurations(E), E' ⊂ E, and N = {X ∈ A : |X| ⊂ E∖E'}, the figurations supported off E'. The expected quotient is A/N = Figurations(E'), presumably via restriction or trace to E'. Figurations not meeting E' go to φ. The last line notes that A/N should be read as a quotient of A∖N rather than a sub-object, i.e. the restriction map A∖N → Fig(E') is surjective and identifies elements.

The next page admits that existence is not obvious, even for 'set-like' ateliers or special N (Ob F, Supp F). It says the case of maquettes, where x ≤ y ⇒ x = y and A/N = A∖N, is easy. Grothendieck then abandons the question ('je n'ai pas la pêche').
errors: No mathematical error. The page is a question plus a heuristic example.
Gap: the existence of A/N is not established, and Grothendieck himself flags uncertainty whether p should kill exactly N or a larger set ⊃N.
Gap: the claim A/N = Figurations(E') is asserted without checking the universal property.

ideas.what: Morphisms of ateliers as partial maps encoded by pointed maps A⊔{φ} → A'⊔{φ} compatible with the structure; kernel = preimage of φ
ideas.modern_name: Partial maps / Kleisli category of the Maybe monad; pointed-set kernels
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (pointed sets, partial-map categories; Robinson–Rosolini on partial maps)

ideas.what: Universal quotient A → A/N annihilating a sub-part N closed under ∘c (cokernel of N ↪ A)
ideas.modern_name: Cokernel in a pointed category; Rees quotient of a semigroup with zero by an ideal; quotient of a space by a closed subspace
ideas.usually_credited_to: Rees (1940) for semigroups; general pointed-category cokernels folklore

ideas.what: Model example: figurations of E modulo those supported in E∖E' give figurations of E', realized as a quotient of A∖N
ideas.modern_name: Restriction to a subspace / localization away from a closed or open part (analogue of j^* or Verdier/Serre quotient)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to stratification ideas in Esquisse d'un programme, but 'ateliers' and 'figurations' are not in published texts as far as I know

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks for the existence and canonicity of quotient ateliers A/N for ∘c-closed parts N. He settles only the trivial maquette case, then abandons the question on the next page.
missed.quote: A --f--> A' annulant une [partie] ⊃ N, se factorise par p de façon unique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of interest if the 'atelier' formalism (an unpublished combinatorial framework from 1986) were revived. Then a kernel/cokernel theory, i.e. a quasi-abelian or 'pointed exact' structure on ateliers, would be the natural first step.

deep.surprise_reason: The page asks for a standard universal construction (a cokernel/Rees-type quotient) in Grothendieck's unpublished 'atelier' framework, with one example. The framework is obscure, but the mathematics on this page is routine and unfinished.
transcription_corrections: '{p}' in A ⊔ {p} and Â should be '{φ}', the null element, consistent with p.6 where f(x) = φ.
'la nullité N' is more likely 'la partie N' (cf. p.6: 'Partons d'une partie N ⊂ A').
The underlined word in the NB is probably 'morphisme' ('La notion de morphisme est claire, en interprétant les morphismes d'ateliers comme des applications ensemblistes'), not 'surjection'.
'ou en termes plus de termes d'ateliers' should probably read 'i.e. tout morphisme d'ateliers'.
The last line likely reads '[A/N] interprété comme quotient de A∖N'.
